metadata.title: Topological Hochschild Homology and Higher Characteristics

nodes.name: bicategory
nodes.statement: A {\bf bicategory} $\mc{B}$ consists of objects, $A, B, \ldots$, called $0$-cells, and categories $\mc{B}(A, B)$ for each pair of objects $A, B$. Objects in the category $\mc{B}(A, B)$ are called 1-cells and morphisms are called 2-cells. The unit $1$-cell associated to a 0-cell $A$ is denoted $U_A$. There are horizontal composition functors \[ \odot \colon \mc{B}(A, B) \times \mc{B}(B, C) \to \mc{B}(A, C). \] They need not be strictly associative or unital.
nodes.statement_short: A bicategory has 0-cells, hom-categories $\mc{B}(A,B)$ whose objects/morphisms are 1-/2-cells, units $U_A$, and a not-necessarily-strict horizontal composition $\odot$.
differentia: objects, $A, B, \ldots$, called $0$-cells, and categories $\mc{B}(A, B)$ for each pair of objects $A, B$
There are horizontal composition functors \[ \odot \colon \mc{B}(A, B) \times \mc{B}(B, C) \to \mc{B}(A, C). \]
They need not be strictly associative or unital.

nodes.name: Reidemeister trace
nodes.statement: For that we need a more powerful invariant: the Reidemeister trace, defined as follows. Let $\{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$ be the set of fixed points of $f$. We say $x_i$ and $x_j$ are in the same fixed point class if there is a path $\gamma$ from $x_i$ to $x_j$ such that $\gamma \simeq f(\gamma)$ relative $\{x_i, x_j\} =\{f(x_i), f(x_j)\}$. This is an equivalence relation which partitions the set of fixed points into fixed point classes, and the free abelian group on fixed point classes is denoted $\mbf{Z}[\pi_1 (X)_f]$. The Reidemeister trace of $f$ is $R(f) = \sum_{x_i} \operatorname{ind}(x_i) [x_i] \in \mbf{Z}[\pi_1 X_f].$ We then have $L(f) = \sum_{x_i} \operatorname{ind}(x_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: The index-weighted sum of fixed point classes of $f$, an element of the free abelian group $\mbf{Z}[\pi_1 X_f]$, refining the Lefschetz number.
nodes.genus: the free abelian group on fixed point classes
differentia: $R(f) = \sum_{x_i} \operatorname{ind}(x_i) [x_i] \in \mbf{Z}[\pi_1 X_f].$

nodes.name: pointwise cofibrant spectral category
nodes.statement: A spectral category $\mc{C}$ is \textbf{pointwise cofibrant} if each mapping spectrum $\mc{C}(a, b)$ is cofibrant in the enriching category.
differentia: each mapping spectrum $\mc{C}(a, b)$ is cofibrant in the enriching category

nodes.name: $\mc{C}$-module
nodes.statement: Let $\mc{C}$ be a spectral category. Then a $\mc{C}$\textbf{-module} is a spectral functor $\mc{C} \to \Sp$.

nodes.name: $(\mc{C}, \mc{D})$-bimodule
nodes.statement: A \textbf{$(\mc{C}, \mc{D})$-bimodule} is a functor $\mc{M}\colon \mc{C}^{\text{op}} \sma \mc{D} \to \Sp$. That is, $\mc{M}$ is a collection of spectra $\mc{M}(c, d)$ for $c \in \mc{C}$, $d \in \mc{D}$ together with maps \begin{align*} &\mc{C}(c, c') \sma \mc{M}(c', d) \to \mc{M}(c, d)\\ &\mc{M}(c, d) \sma \mc{D}(d,d') \to \mc{M}(c, d') \end{align*} An $(\mc{C}, \mc{D})$-bimodule is {\bf pointwise cofibrant} if $\mc{M}(c, d)$ is cofibrant. A {\bf morphism} of $(\mc{C}, \mc{D})$-bimodules $\mc{M} \to \mc{M}'$ is a collection of maps $\mc{M}(c, d) \to \mc{M}'(c, d)$ which commute with the appropriate structure.
nodes.statement_short: A spectrally enriched functor $\mc{C}^{op} \sma \mc{D} \to \Sp$, i.e. spectra $\mc{M}(c,d)$ with compatible left $\mc{C}$- and right $\mc{D}$-actions.
differentia: a collection of spectra $\mc{M}(c, d)$ for $c \in \mc{C}$, $d \in \mc{D}$ together with maps \begin{align*} &\mc{C}(c, c') \sma \mc{M}(c', d) \to \mc{M}(c, d)\\ &\mc{M}(c, d) \sma \mc{D}(d,d') \to \mc{M}(c, d') \end{align*}

nodes.name: topological Hochschild homology of $\mc{C}$ with coefficients in $\mc{Q}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mc{C}$ be a pointwise cofibrant spectral category, and $\mc{Q}$ a $(\mc{C},\mc{C})$-bimodule. The \textbf{topological Hochschild homology of $\mc{C}$ with coefficients in $\mc{Q}$} is the geometric realization of a spectrum whose $n$th simplicial level is \[ \thh(\mc{C}; \mc{Q})_n \coloneqq N^{\text{cy}}_n (\mc{C}, \mc{Q}) = \bigvee_{c_0, \dots, c_n} \mc{C}(c_0, c_1) \sma \mc{C}(c_1, c_2) \sma \cdots \sma \mc{C}(c_{n-1}, c_n) \sma \mc{Q}(c_n, c_0) \] That is, \[ \thh(\mc{C};\mc{Q}) \coloneqq \vert\thh(\mc{C};\mc{Q})_\bullet\vert \]
nodes.statement_short: $\thh(\mc{C};\mc{Q})$ is the realization of the cyclic nerve $N^{cy}_\bullet(\mc{C},\mc{Q})$ built from smash products of mapping spectra ending in $\mc{Q}$.
nodes.definiendum: topological Hochschild homology of $\mc{C}$ with coefficients in $\mc{Q}$
differentia: whose $n$th simplicial level is \[ \thh(\mc{C}; \mc{Q})_n \coloneqq N^{\text{cy}}_n (\mc{C}, \mc{Q}) = \bigvee_{c_0, \dots, c_n} \mc{C}(c_0, c_1) \sma \mc{C}(c_1, c_2) \sma \cdots \sma \mc{C}(c_{n-1}, c_n) \sma \mc{Q}(c_n, c_0) \]

nodes.name: base change bimodule $\ _F \mc{C}_G$
nodes.statement: Let $F\colon \mc{A} \to \mc{C}$ and $G\colon \mc{B} \to \mc{C}$ be functors between spectral categories. Define an $(\mc{A}, \mc{B})$-bimodule $ \ _F \mc{C}_G$ as follows. For objects $a\in \mc{A}$ and $b \in \mc{B}$ \[ \ _F \mc{C}_G (a, b) \coloneqq \mc{C}(F(a), G(b)). \] The right action of $\mc{B}$ on $\ _F \mc{C}_G$ is given by the functor $G$: \begin{align*} \ _F \mc{C}_G(a, b) \sma \mc{B} (b, b') &= \mc{C}(F(a),G(b)) \sma \mc{B} (b, b') \to \mc{C}(F(a), G(b)) \sma \mc{C}(G(b), G(b'))\\ &\to \mc{C} (F(a), G(b')) = \ _F \mc{C}_G (a, b') \end{align*} The left action of $\mc{A}$ is similar.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the mapping spectra of $\mc{C}$ along two functors $F$, $G$ to get an $(\mc{A},\mc{B})$-bimodule $\ _F\mc{C}_G(a,b) = \mc{C}(F(a),G(b))$.
differentia: \ _F \mc{C}_G (a, b) \coloneqq \mc{C}(F(a), G(b)).

nodes.name: right twisted topological Hochschild homology
nodes.statement: Let $\mc{C}$ be a pointwise cofibrant spectral category and $F\colon \mc{C} \to \mc{C}$ be an endofunctor. We defined the \textbf{right twisted topological Hochschild homology} to be \[ \thh(\mc{C}; F)\coloneqq\thh(\mc{C}; \mc{C}_F) \]
differentia: $F\colon \mc{C} \to \mc{C}$ be an endofunctor

nodes.name: bicategory of small spectral categories
nodes.statement: The bicategory of small spectral categories is the bicategory whose objects are pointwise cofibrant small spectral categories, and whose morphism categories are \[ \operatorname{Ho}\left(\operatorname{Mod}_{(\mc{C}, \mc{D})}\right) \] for pointwise cofibrant small spectral categories $\mc{C}$ and $\mc{D}$.
differentia: whose objects are pointwise cofibrant small spectral categories
whose morphism categories are \[ \operatorname{Ho}\left(\operatorname{Mod}_{(\mc{C}, \mc{D})}\right) \]

nodes.name: shadow functor
nodes.statement: Let $\mc{B}$ be a bicategory. A \textbf{shadow functor} for $\mc{B}$ consists of functors \[ \sh{-}\colon \mc{B}(C,C) \to \mbf{T} \] for each object $C$ of $\mc{B}$ and some fixed category $\mbf{T}$, equipped with a natural isomorphism \[ \theta\colon \sh{M\odot N}\xto{\cong} \sh{N\odot M} \] for $M\in \mc{B}(C, D)$ and $N\in \mc{B}(D, C)$ such that the following diagrams commute whenever they make sense: \[\xymatrix{ \sh{(M\odot N)\odot P} \ar[r]^\theta \ar[d]_{\sh{a}} & \sh{P \odot (M\odot N)} \ar[r]^{\sh{a}} & \sh{(P\odot M) \odot N} \\ \sh{M\odot (N\odot P)} \ar[r]^\theta & \sh{(N\odot P)\odot M} \ar[r]^{\sh{a}} & \sh{N\odot (P\odot M)}\ar[u]_\theta }\] \[\xymatrix{ \sh{M\odot U_C} \ar[r]^\theta \ar[dr]_{\sh{r}} & \sh{U_C\odot M} \ar[d]^{\sh{l}} \ar[r]^\theta & \sh{M\odot U_C} \ar[dl]^{\sh{r}} \\ &\sh{M}}\]
nodes.statement_short: Functors $\sh{-}\colon \mc{B}(C,C)\to \mbf{T}$ with a cyclic-invariance isomorphism $\theta\colon\sh{M\odot N}\cong\sh{N\odot M}$ compatible with associativity and units.
nodes.genus: functors \[ \sh{-}\colon \mc{B}(C,C) \to \mbf{T} \] for each object $C$ of $\mc{B}$ and some fixed category $\mbf{T}$
differentia: equipped with a natural isomorphism \[ \theta\colon \sh{M\odot N}\xto{\cong} \sh{N\odot M} \] for $M\in \mc{B}(C, D)$ and $N\in \mc{B}(D, C)$
such that the following diagrams commute whenever they make sense

nodes.name: the bicategories $\mc{B}(\mathbf{Mon}(\mc{V}))$ and $\mc{B}(\mathbf{Cat}(\mc{V}))$
nodes.statement: Let $\mc{V}$ be a symmetric monoidal category. (In what follows, one can imagine that $\mc{V}$ is the category of spectra.) \begin{enumerate} \item Let $\mc{B}(\mathbf{Mon}(\mc{V}))$ be the bicategory whose objects are monoids in $\mc{V}$, 1-cells are bimodules over monoids in $\mc{V}$ and whose 2-cells are maps of bimodules. \item Let $\mc{B}(\mathbf{Cat}(\mc{V}))$ be the bicategory whose objects are categories enriched in $\mc{V}$, whose 1-cells are functors $F \colon \mc{C}^{\text{op}} \otimes \mc{D} \to \mc{V}$ (also known as $(\mc{C}, \mc{D})$-bimodules) and whose 2-cells are natural transformations of such. \end{enumerate} These bicategories both have shadows that take values in $\mc{V}$.
nodes.statement_short: The two running example bicategories: monoids in $\mc{V}$ with bimodules, and $\mc{V}$-enriched categories with bimodules; both carry shadows valued in $\mc{V}$.

nodes.name: right dualizable 1-cell, dual pair
nodes.statement: We say that a 1-cell $M\in \mc{B}(C,D)$ in a bicategory is \textbf{right dualizable} if there is a 1-cell $N\in \mc{B}(D,C)$, called its \textbf{right dual}, and coevaluation and evaluation 2-cells $\eta\colon U_C \to M\odot N$ and $\epsilon \colon N\odot M\to U_D$ satisfying the triangle identities. We say that $(M,N)$ is a \textbf{dual pair}, that $N$ is \textbf{left dualizable}, and that $M$ is its \textbf{left dual}.
nodes.statement_short: $M$ is right dualizable when it admits a right dual $N$ with coevaluation $\eta$ and evaluation $\epsilon$ satisfying the triangle identities.
differentia: there is a 1-cell $N\in \mc{B}(D,C)$, called its \textbf{right dual}, and coevaluation and evaluation 2-cells $\eta\colon U_C \to M\odot N$ and $\epsilon \colon N\odot M\to U_D$ satisfying the triangle identities

nodes.name: trace of a 2-cell (bicategorical trace)
nodes.statement: Let $\mc{B}$ be a bicategory with a shadow functor and $(M,N)$ be a dual pair. The \textbf{trace} of a 2-cell $f\colon Q\odot M\rightarrow M\odot P$ is the composite: \[ \sh{Q}\cong \sh{Q\odot U_C}\xto{\sh{\id_Q\odot\eta}} \sh{Q\odot M\odot N} \xto{\sh{f\odot\id_N}} \sh{M\odot P\odot N} \xto{\theta} \sh{N\odot M\odot P} \xto{\sh{\epsilon \odot \id_P}} \sh{U_D\odot P}\cong \sh{P}. \] The trace of a 2-cell $g\colon N\odot Q\to P\odot N$ is \[ \sh{Q}\cong \sh{U_C\odot Q}\xto{\sh{\eta\odot\id_Q}} \sh{M\odot N\odot Q} \xto{\sh{\id_M\odot g}} \sh{M\odot P\odot N} \xto{\theta} \sh{P\odot N\odot M} \xto{\sh{\id_P \odot \epsilon}} \sh{P\odot U_D}\cong \sh{P}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The bicategorical trace of $f\colon Q\odot M\to M\odot P$ is the shadow-level composite built from $\eta$, $f$, cyclic invariance $\theta$, and $\epsilon$.
differentia: \sh{Q}\cong \sh{Q\odot U_C}\xto{\sh{\id_Q\odot\eta}} \sh{Q\odot M\odot N} \xto{\sh{f\odot\id_N}} \sh{M\odot P\odot N} \xto{\theta} \sh{N\odot M\odot P} \xto{\sh{\epsilon \odot \id_P}} \sh{U_D\odot P}\cong \sh{P}.

nodes.name: notation $\rsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}$, $\rsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P}$, $\lsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}$, $\lsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P}$
nodes.statement: Let $(M,N)$ be a dual pair and $Q$ and $P$ be 1-cells so that $N\odot Q\odot M$ and $M\odot P\odot N$ are defined. We then fix the following notation: \begin{gather*} \rsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}\colon Q\odot M\cong U_C\odot Q\odot M \xto{\eta\odot \id_Q\odot \id_M} M\odot N\odot Q\odot M \\ \rsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P}\colon M\odot P\odot N\odot M \xto{\id_M \odot \id_P \odot\epsilon} M\odot P\odot U_D\cong M\odot P \\ \lsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q} \colon N\odot Q\cong N\odot Q\odot U_C \xto{\id_N\odot \id_Q\odot \eta} N\odot Q\odot M\odot N \\ \lsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P}\colon N\odot M\odot P\odot N \xto{\epsilon\odot \id_P \odot \id_N } U_D\odot P\odot N\cong P\odot N \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Notation for the four 2-cells obtained by inserting $\eta$ or applying $\epsilon$ on the left or right of a dual pair.

nodes.name: dual $g^\star$ of a map
nodes.statement: If $(M,N)$ is a dual pair, the {\bf dual} of a map $g\colon N\odot Q\to P\odot N$, denoted $g^\star$, is the composite \begin{align*} Q\odot M\xto{\rsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}} M\odot N\odot Q\odot M\xto{\id_M \odot g\odot \id_M}M\odot P\odot N\odot M \xto{\rsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P} } M\odot P \end{align*} Since $\tr(g)=\tr(g^\star)$ \cite[Prop.~7.6]{ps:bicat} we freely move between traces defined with respect to $M$ and those defined with respect to $N$. Note that $\rsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}$ is the dual of $\lsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}$, $\rsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{Q}$ is the dual of $\lsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{Q}$, and \begin{gather*} \sh{Q}\xto{\tr\left(\rsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}\right)=\tr\left(\lsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}\right)} \sh{N\odot Q\odot M} \quad \text{and } \quad \sh{M\odot P\odot N}\xto{\tr\left(\rsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P}\right)=\tr\left(\lsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P}\right)} \sh{P} \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: The dual $g^\star$ of $g\colon N\odot Q\to P\odot N$ has the same trace, so traces may be computed with respect to either member of the dual pair.
differentia: Q\odot M\xto{\rsm{\eta}{M}{N}{Q}} M\odot N\odot Q\odot M\xto{\id_M \odot g\odot \id_M}M\odot P\odot N\odot M \xto{\rsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P} } M\odot P

nodes.name: Euler characteristic
nodes.statement: If $M\in \mc{B}(C,D)$ and $M$ is right dualizable, the \textbf{Euler characteristic} (\cref{fig:euler_char}) is the trace of the identity 2-cell of $M$ and is a map \[\sh{U_C}\to \sh{U_D}.\] If $N$ is the right dual of $M$, $\chi(M)=\chi(N)$.
nodes.statement_short: The bicategorical Euler characteristic of a right dualizable 1-cell is the trace of its identity 2-cell, a map $\sh{U_C}\to\sh{U_D}$.
nodes.genus: the trace of the identity 2-cell of $M$
differentia: $M\in \mc{B}(C,D)$ and $M$ is right dualizable

nodes.name: Morita equivalence (of 1-cells)
nodes.statement: A pair of one cells $M\in \mc{B}(C,D)$ and $N\in \mc{B}(D,C)$ is a {\bf Morita equivalence} if $(M,N)$ and $(N,M)$ are dual pairs and the coevaluation and evaluation maps for each dual pair are inverses. That is, if $\eta_{(M,N)}$ and $\epsilon_{(M,N)}$ are the coevaluation and evaluation for $(M,N)$ and $\eta_{(N,M)}$ and $\epsilon_{(N,M)}$ are the coevaluation and evaluation for $(N,M)$ then \begin{align*} \eta_{(N,M)}\circ \epsilon_{(M,N)}=\id_{N\odot M} &\qquad \epsilon_{(N,M)}\circ \eta_{(M,N)}=\id_{U_{C}} \\ \eta_{(M,N)}\circ \epsilon_{(N,M)}=\id_{M\odot N}&\qquad \epsilon_{(M,N)}\circ \eta_{(N,M)}=\id_{U_{{D}}} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A Morita equivalence is a pair $(M,N)$ that is a dual pair in both orders, with the two coevaluations and evaluations mutually inverse.
differentia: $(M,N)$ and $(N,M)$ are dual pairs
the coevaluation and evaluation maps for each dual pair are inverses

nodes.name: Morita equivalent 0-cells
nodes.statement: If $M \in \mc{B}(C, D)$ and $N \in \mc{B}(D, C)$ define a Morita equivalence, then $C$ and $D$ are said to be \textbf{Morita equivalent}.
differentia: $M \in \mc{B}(C, D)$ and $N \in \mc{B}(D, C)$ define a Morita equivalence

nodes.name: base change bimodules $_f C$ and $C_f$ for a monoid map
nodes.section: 5.1 Morita equivalence arising from base change
nodes.statement: Let $f\colon A \to C$ be a morphism in $\mbf{Mon}(\mc{V})$. Then there is an $(A, C)$-bimodule $ _f C$, which is $C$ with a left $A$-action given by $f$, and a $(C, A)$-bimodule $C_f$ which is $C$ with a right $A$-action given by $f$.
differentia: $C$ with a left $A$-action given by $f$
$C$ with a right $A$-action given by $f$

nodes.name: base change bimodule $_F \mc{C}$ for an enriched functor
nodes.section: 5.1 Morita equivalence arising from base change
nodes.statement: Let $F\colon \mc{A} \to \mc{C}$ be a morphism in $\mbf{Cat}(\mc{V})$, i.e. a functor of categories enriched in $\mc{V}$. Then there is an $(\mc{A}, \mc{C})$-bimodule $_F \mc{C}$ where the left action of $\mc{A}$ is given by \begin{align*} \mc{A}(a, a') \otimes ({_F \mc{C}})(a', c) &= \mc{A}(a, a') \otimes \mc{C}(F(a'), c) \\ &\to \mc{C}(F(a), F(a')) \otimes \mc{C}(F(a'), c) \to \mc{C}(F(a), c) = {_F \mc{C}(a, c)} \end{align*} There is a dual $(\mc{C}, \mc{A})$-bimodule that we denote $\mc{C}_F$.
nodes.statement_short: Restriction along an enriched functor $F$ gives an $(\mc{A},\mc{C})$-bimodule $_F\mc{C}$ and dually a $(\mc{C},\mc{A})$-bimodule $\mc{C}_F$.
differentia: the left action of $\mc{A}$ is given by \begin{align*} \mc{A}(a, a') \otimes ({_F \mc{C}})(a', c) &= \mc{A}(a, a') \otimes \mc{C}(F(a'), c) \\ &\to \mc{C}(F(a), F(a')) \otimes \mc{C}(F(a'), c) \to \mc{C}(F(a), c) = {_F \mc{C}(a, c)} \end{align*}

nodes.name: base change 1-cells
nodes.section: 5.1 Morita equivalence arising from base change
nodes.statement: We call any of $_f C$, $C_f$, $_F \mc{C}$, $\mc{C}_F$ \textbf{base change 1-cells}.

nodes.name: Morita equivalence of a $\sV$-functor
nodes.section: 5.1 Morita equivalence arising from base change
nodes.statement: A $\sV$-functor $F\colon \sA\to \sC$ is a {\bf Morita equivalence} if $({_F\sC},\sC_F)$ is a Morita equivalence. In particular, $F$ is a Morita equivalence if and only if $F$ is full and faithful and the map induced by composition \[ \sC(c,F(-))\odot\sC(F(-),c')\to \sC(c,c') \] is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: A $\sV$-functor is a Morita equivalence when its base change pair is one; equivalently, it is fully faithful and composition induces an isomorphism.
differentia: $({_F\sC},\sC_F)$ is a Morita equivalence
$F$ is full and faithful and the map induced by composition \[ \sC(c,F(-))\odot\sC(F(-),c')\to \sC(c,c') \] is an isomorphism

nodes.name: restricted bimodule ${_F\mc{M}_G}$ and the maps $\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}$
nodes.section: 5.1 Morita equivalence arising from base change
nodes.statement: If $\mc{M}$ is a $(\mc{C},\mc{D})$-bimodule and $F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}$ and $G\colon \mc{B}\to \mc{D}$ are enriched functors, ${_F\mc{M}_G}$ is the $(\mc{A},\mc{B})$-bimodule defined as the composite \[ \mc{A}^{\text{op}}\otimes \mc{B}\xto{F\otimes G}\mc{C}^{\text{op}}\otimes \mc{D}\xto{\mc{M}}\mc{V} \] If $\mc{Q}$ is an $(\mc{C},\mc{C})$-bimodule and $F$ is as above, we have the following composite \[ \rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}\colon {_F\mc{Q}_F}\odot {_F\mc{C}} \cong {_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{Q}\odot \mc{C}_F\odot {_F\mc{C}} \xto{\rsm{\epsilon}{_F\mc{C}}{\mc{C}_F}{\mc{Q}}}{_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{Q} \] and the corresponding maps for $\rbm{\eta}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}$, $\lbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}$, and $\lbm{\eta}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}$. The are also versions of these maps for monoids.
nodes.statement_short: Restriction of a bimodule along two functors, and the evaluation-type 2-cells $\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}$ obtained from the base change dual pair.
differentia: defined as the composite \[ \mc{A}^{\text{op}}\otimes \mc{B}\xto{F\otimes G}\mc{C}^{\text{op}}\otimes \mc{D}\xto{\mc{M}}\mc{V} \]

nodes.name: $\End_\mc{C}(c)$ and the inclusion $E_c$
nodes.statement: If $\mc{C}$ is a category enriched in $\mc{V}$ and $c$ is an object of $\mc{C}$ let $\End_\mc{C}(c)$ denote the full subcategory of $\mc{C}$ whose single object is $c$. Let $E_c\colon \End_\mc{C}(c)\to \mc{C}$ be the inclusion.
differentia: whose single object is $c$

nodes.name: the 2-cells $\phi$ and $\psi$ associated to a natural transformation $\Phi$
nodes.statement: For enriched categories $\mc{A}$ and $\mc{C}$, enriched functors \[ J\colon \mc{A}\to\mc{A}, K\colon \mc{C}\to \mc{C}\text{ and }F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}, \] and a natural transformation $\Phi\colon F\circ J\to K\circ F$ let $\phi\colon \mc{A}_{J}\odot {_F\mc{C}} \to {_F\mc{C}\odot\mc{C}_K }$ be the 2-cell defined by \begin{align*} (a\xto{\alpha}J(a'),F(a')\xto{\beta}c)&\mapsto (F(a)\xto{F(\alpha)}F(J(a'))\xto{ \Phi_{a'}}K(F(a'))\xto{K(\beta)}K(c)) \end{align*} and $\psi\colon \mc{A}_J\to{_F\mc{C}\odot \mc{C}_K\odot \mc{C}_F} $ be 2-cell defined by \[ (a\xto{\alpha} J(a'))\mapsto (F(a)\xto{F(\alpha)}F(J(a'))\xto{\Phi_{a'}}K(F(a'))) \] This choice of $\phi$ and $\psi$ are related as in \eqref{switch_for_trace}.
nodes.statement_short: A natural transformation $\Phi\colon F\circ J\to K\circ F$ induces base change 2-cells $\phi$ and $\psi$ by composing with $F(\alpha)$, $\Phi$ and $K(\beta)$.

nodes.name: restriction and transfer
nodes.statement: Letting $R$ be the sphere spectrum and taking $\thh$ of both sides of the adjunction gives us maps \[ \operatorname{res}\colon \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{A}) \leftrightarrows \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_C) \colon \operatorname{trf} \] which are usually referred to as \textbf{restriction} and \textbf{transfer}. There is a restriction for any map $f$, but there is only a transfer if $C$ is compact as an $A$-module. Using Morita invariance restriction and transfer give maps between $\thh(A)$ and $\thh(C)$.
nodes.statement_short: Applying $\thh$ to the base change adjunction gives restriction and transfer maps between $\thh(\Mod^c_A)$ and $\thh(\Mod^c_C)$.
differentia: There is a restriction for any map $f$, but there is only a transfer if $C$ is compact as an $A$-module.

nodes.name: the bimodule map $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}$
nodes.statement: If $\mc{M}$ is an $(\mc{C},\mc{D})$-bimodule and $F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}$ is a functor let $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}$ be the $(\mc{A},\mc{D})$-bimodule map given by composite \[_F\mc{C}_F\odot {_F\mc{M}}\xleftarrow{\id_{_F\mc{C}_F}\odot \sim } {_F\mc{C}_F}\odot {_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{M} \xto{\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_{\mc{C}}}\odot \id_\mc{M}} {_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{M} \xto{\sim } {_F\mc{M}}\] This map is induced by the action of $\mc{C}$ on $\mc{M}$ restricted to the objects in the image of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: The $(\mc{A},\mc{D})$-bimodule map given by the action of $\mc{C}$ on $\mc{M}$ restricted along $F$.

nodes.name: the categories $1_{\mc{C}}$ and the functors $I$, $I_c$
nodes.statement: If $\mc{C}$ is a category enriched in $\mc{V}$, let $1_{\mc{C}}$ be the category whose objects are the objects of $\mc{C}$ and \[1_{\mc{C}}(c,c')=\left\{\begin{array}{cc} 1_\mc{V}&\text{if }c=c' \\ \emptyset &\text{if } c\neq c'\end{array}\right.\] The composition map is the unit isomorphism. Let $I\colon 1_\mc{C}\to \mc{C}$ be the functor that picks out the identity map for each $c\in \mc{C}$. If $c$ is an object of $\mc{C}$, and we regard $1_{\mc{V}}$ as a one object category with object $\ast$, there is a functor $I_c\colon 1_\mc{V}\to 1_\mc{C}\to \mc{C}$ that picks out the identity map of $c$.
nodes.statement_short: $1_\mc{C}$ is the discrete $\mc{V}$-category on the objects of $\mc{C}$, with functors $I$ and $I_c$ picking out identity maps.
differentia: whose objects are the objects of $\mc{C}$ and \[1_{\mc{C}}(c,c')=\left\{\begin{array}{cc} 1_\mc{V}&\text{if }c=c' \\ \emptyset &\text{if } c\neq c'\end{array}\right.\]

nodes.name: free Moore path space
nodes.statement: The \textbf{free Moore path space} is defined to be \[ \mc{P}^M X = \{(\gamma, u) \in \operatorname{Map}([0, \infty), X) \times [0, \infty) : \gamma(t) = \gamma(u) \ t \geq u \}. \] Here $\operatorname{Map}([0,\infty), X)$ is given the compact open topology. The space $\mc{P}^M X$ comes equipped with two maps $s\colon \mc{P}^M X \to X$ and $t\colon \mc{P}^M X \to X$ given by evaluation at $0$ and $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Paths of variable length $u$ in $X$ that are constant after time $u$, with source and target evaluation maps.
differentia: \gamma(t) = \gamma(u) \ t \geq u

nodes.name: Moore loop space
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a based space with base $\ast$. Then the \textbf{Moore loop space} is \[ \Omega^M X = \{(\gamma, u) \in \mc{P}^M X : \gamma(0) = \gamma(u) = \ast\} \] that is, it is the pullback \[ \xymatrix{ \Omega^M X \ar[r]\ar[d] & \mc{P}^MX \ar[d]^{s \times t} \\ \ast\ar[r] & X \times X } \] For work below, it is convenient to denote the ``length'' of the path, $u$, by $|\omega|$.
differentia: \gamma(0) = \gamma(u) = \ast

nodes.name: $f$-twisted Moore loop space
nodes.statement: The \textbf{$f$-twisted Moore loop space} is the topological space \[ \Omega^M X^f = \{(\gamma, u) \in \mc{P}^M X : \gamma(0) = \ast, \gamma(u) = f(\ast)\} \] i.e. it is given as a pullback \[ \xymatrix{ \Omega^M X^f \ar[r]\ar[d] & \mc{P}^M X \ar[d]\\ \ast \ar[r]^{\operatorname{id} \times f} & X \times X } \] Again, $|\omega|$ denotes the length of the path $\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: Moore paths starting at $\ast$ and ending at $f(\ast)$.
differentia: \gamma(0) = \ast, \gamma(u) = f(\ast)

nodes.name: bimodule structure on $\Omega^M X^f$
nodes.statement: This space $\Omega^M X^f$ is homotopy equivalent to $\Omega^M X$ and has the structure of an \\$(\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X)$-bimodule. For $\alpha \in \Omega^M X$, $\gamma\in \Omega^M X^f$ and $\beta \in \Omega^M X$ \[ \alpha \cdot \gamma = \alpha \ast \gamma \qquad \gamma \cdot \beta = \gamma \ast f(\beta) \]
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega^M X^f$ is an $(\Omega^M X,\Omega^M X)$-bimodule with right action twisted by $f$.
differentia: \alpha \cdot \gamma = \alpha \ast \gamma \qquad \gamma \cdot \beta = \gamma \ast f(\beta)

nodes.name: $f$-twisted free loop space
nodes.statement: The \textbf{$f$-twisted free loop space} is defined to be \[ \mc{L} X^f = \{\gamma \in \mc{P} X : \gamma(0) = f(\gamma(1))\} \] That is, $\mc{L} X^f$ arises as the pullback \[ \xymatrix{ \mc{L} X^f \ar[d]\ar[r] & \mc{P} X \ar[d]^{\operatorname{ev}_0 \times \operatorname{ev}_1}\\ X \ar[r]^{\operatorname{id} \times f} & X \times X } \] Consequently, $\mc{L}^f X$ sits in a fibration sequence \[ \Omega X^f \to \mc{L}^f X \to X \]
nodes.statement_short: Paths $\gamma$ in $X$ with $\gamma(0)=f(\gamma(1))$; it fibers over $X$ with fiber $\Omega X^f$.
differentia: \gamma(0) = f(\gamma(1))

nodes.name: $N^{\text{cy}} (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f)$
nodes.statement: $N^{\text{cy}} (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f)$ is the geometric realization of the simplicial space with $n$-simplices \[ N^{\text{cy}}_n (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) = \underbrace{\Omega^M X \times \cdots \times \Omega^M X}_{n\ \text{times}} \times \Omega^M X^f \] The face maps $d_i \colon N^{\text{cy}}_n \to N^{\text{cy}}_{n-1}$ are given by \[ d_i (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega) = \begin{cases} (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_i \omega_{i+1}, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega) & i < n \\ (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1} \omega) & i = n \\ (\omega_1, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega f(\omega_0)) & i = n+1 \end{cases} \] The degeneracies $s_j \colon N^{cy}_{n} \to N^{\text{cy}}_{n+1}$ are given by the insertion of trivial paths: \[ s_j (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega) = (\cdots, \omega_{j}, \ast, \omega_{j+1}, \dots) \]
nodes.statement_short: The $f$-twisted cyclic bar construction on $\Omega^M X$, whose last face map inserts $f(\omega_0)$.
nodes.genus: geometric realization of the simplicial space
differentia: N^{\text{cy}}_n (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) = \underbrace{\Omega^M X \times \cdots \times \Omega^M X}_{n\ \text{times}} \times \Omega^M X^f

nodes.name: $(\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^n}$
nodes.statement: The space $(\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^n}$ is defined to be \[ (\Omega X^f )^{\Delta^n} = \left\{\gamma \in \operatorname{Map}(\Delta^n, \mc{P} X) \biggr| \begin{matrix}\gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (0) = \ast, \gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n}(1) = f(\ast)\\ \text{for all}\ (u_0, \dots, u_n) \in \Delta^n \end{matrix}\right\} \] The cosimplicial structure on $\Delta^\bullet$ induces a simplicial structure on $(\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^\bullet}$. The face maps are given by restriction: \[ d_i (\gamma)(t, u_0, \dots, u_n) = \gamma(t, u_0, \dots,u_i, 0, u_{i+1}, \dots, u_n) \] where $t$ is the path coordinate and the degeneracy maps are given by addition of coordinates: \[ s_i (\gamma)(t, u_0, \dots, u_n) = \gamma(t, u_0, \dots, u_i + u_{i+1}, \dots, u_n) \]
nodes.statement_short: Simplices worth of twisted loops: maps $\Delta^n\to\mc{P}X$ whose every path runs from $\ast$ to $f(\ast)$.
differentia: \gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (0) = \ast, \gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n}(1) = f(\ast)

nodes.name: $(\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^n}$
nodes.statement: The topological space $(\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^n}$ is defined to be \[ (\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^n} = \left\{\gamma \in \operatorname{Map}(\Delta^n, \mc{P} X)\biggr|\begin{matrix} \gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (0) = f (\gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (1)) \\ \text{for all}\ (u_0, \dots, u_n) \in \Delta^n \end{matrix}\right\} \] Again, the cosimplicial structure on $\Delta^\bullet$ induces a simplicial structure on $(\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^\bullet}$. The face and degeneracy maps are as above.
differentia: \gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (0) = f (\gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (1))

nodes.name: the comparison maps $A$, $B$, $C$, $i_\bullet$, $p_\bullet$
nodes.statement: We now write out all of the maps in the diagram: \begin{itemize} \item The map \[ A \colon (\Omega^M X^f)_{n,c} \to (\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^n} \] is given by reparamterizing the loops: \[ A (\omega) (t, u_0, \dots, u_n) = \omega(t|\omega|) \] \item The map \[ B \colon N^{\text{cy}}_{n} (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) \to (\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^n} \] is given by: \begin{align*} &B(\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega)(t, u_0, \dots, u_n) \\ &= \widetilde{\omega}\biggl(t (|\omega_0| + |\omega_1| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}| + |\omega|)\\ &+ u_0 (|\omega_0| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|) + u_1 (|\omega_1| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|) \cdots + u_{n-1} (|\omega_{n-1}|)\biggr) \end{align*} where \[ \widetilde{\omega} = \omega_0 \ast \cdots \ast \omega_{n-1} \ast \omega \ast f(\omega_0) \ast f(\omega_1) \cdots \cdots \ast f(\omega_{n-1}) \] \item The map \[ C\colon B_n \Omega^M X \to X^{\Delta^n} \] is given by \begin{align*} &C(\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})(u_0, \dots, u_n)\\ &= (\omega_1 \ast \cdots \ast \omega_n)\biggl( u_0 (|\omega_0| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|) +u_1 (|\omega_1| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|)+ \cdots+ u_{n} (|\omega_{n-1}|)\biggr) \end{align*} \item The maps $i^{\Delta^\bullet}$ and $p^{\Delta^\bullet}$ the obvious ones induced by maps on spaces. \item The map $i_\bullet$ is given level-wise as \[ i_n (\omega) = (\ast, \dots, \ast, \omega) \] and $p_\bullet$ is given level-wise as \[ p_n (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega_n) = (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}) \] \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for the horizontal comparison maps $A$, $B$, $C$ (reparametrizing concatenated loops) and the vertical maps $i_\bullet$, $p_\bullet$.

nodes.name: $\mc{V}$ is a symmetric monoidal category
nodes.section: 5.1 Morita equivalence arising from base change
nodes.statement: In what follows, let $\mc{V}$ be a symmetric monoidal category.

nodes.name: $R$-algebras $A$, $C$ and the base change adjunction
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a ring spectrum and $A$, $C$ be $R$-algebras. A map of $R$-algebras $f\colon A \to C$ defines an $(A, C)$-bimodule $_fC$. If $_fC$ is left dualizable, we have an adjunction \[ C_f \sma_A - \colon \operatorname{Mod}^{lc}_{(A, R)} \leftrightarrows \operatorname{Mod}^{lc}_{(C, R)} \colon \ _f C \sma_C - \] between the bimodules that are left-compact (that is, for example, an $(A, R)$-bimodule is compact when considered as an $A$-module).
nodes.statement_short: A map of $R$-algebras with $_fC$ left dualizable yields an adjunction between left-compact bimodule categories.

nodes.name: commuting square of algebra maps inducing the twisted transfer
nodes.statement: For algebras $A$ and $C$, a commuting diagram of maps of algebra \[\xymatrix{A\ar[r]^j\ar[d]^f&A\ar[d]^f\\C\ar[r]^k&C}\] defines a commuting diagram of functors \[\xymatrix{ \Mod_C^c\ar[d]_-{-\sma_C C_f}\ar[r]^-{-\sma_C C_k}&\Mod_C^c\ar[d]^-{-\sma_C C_f} \\ \Mod_A^c\ar[r]^-{-\sma_A A_j}&\Mod_A^c} \]
nodes.statement_short: A commuting square of algebra self-maps $j$, $k$ over $f$ induces a commuting square of base change functors.

nodes.name: $X$ a finite CW-type path-connected space with self-map $f$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be path-connected space that has the homotopy type of a finite CW-complex, and let $f\colon X \to X$ be a self map. The map $X \to \ast$ gives a map $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X \to S$ which exhibits $S$ as a compact $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X$-module, and so there is a transfer $S \to \thh(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X)$. Also, $f$ induces a self-map $f\colon \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X \to \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X$.
nodes.statement_short: Setup for the main application: $X$ of finite CW type with self-map $f$, giving compactness of $S$ over $\Sigma^\infty_+\Omega X$ and hence a transfer.

nodes.name: Which element of $\pi_0 \operatorname{THH}(A)$ does an endomorphism determine?
nodes.statement: yielding a map $S \to \operatorname{THH}(A)$, i.e. an element of $\pi_0 \operatorname{THH}(A)$. The question is: What element of $\pi_0 \operatorname{THH}(A)$ does $f$ determine? Intuitively, the answer should clearly be $\operatorname{tr}(f)$, but it is far from obvious given how we have defined it. It is therefore desirable to have an actual proof of this, and a categorical proof is even better.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the class in $\pi_0\thh(A)$ that an endomorphism $f$ of a compact $A$-module determines via the inclusion-of-objects map.

nodes.name: Twisted $\thh$ computations for arbitrary self-maps of ring spectra
nodes.statement: It is probable that computations of this sort for arbitrary self-maps of ring spectra, $g\colon A \to A$, are interesting; but we content ourselves with the current example.
nodes.statement_short: Computing twisted $\thh$ for arbitrary ring spectrum self-maps is left untouched.

nodes.name: Reidemeister trace is the $\thh$ transfer
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space homotopy equivalent to a finite CW-complex. The Reidemeister trace is naturally equivalent to the $\thh$ transfer \[ \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_S) \to \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X})\to \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X}; F). \]
nodes.statement_short: For $X$ of finite CW type the Reidemeister trace is the transfer in (twisted) topological Hochschild homology.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a topological space homotopy equivalent to a finite CW-complex.
conclusions: The Reidemeister trace is naturally equivalent to the $\thh$ transfer \[ \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_S) \to \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X})\to \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X}; F). \]

nodes.name: Image of $[f]$ under Morita invariance is the bicategorical trace
nodes.statement: The image of $[f] \in \pi_0 \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_A)$ under the Morita invariance isomorphism \[ \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_A) \simeq \thh(A) \] is the bicategorical trace of $f$. In particular, for a module $M \in \operatorname{Mod}^c_A$, the image of $[\operatorname{id}_M]$ is $\chi(M)$.
nodes.statement_short: Morita invariance sends the class of an endomorphism $f$ to its bicategorical trace, and $[\id_M]$ to $\chi(M)$.
assumptions: The image of $[f] \in \pi_0 \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_A)$ under the Morita invariance isomorphism \[ \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_A) \simeq \thh(A) \]
conclusions: is the bicategorical trace of $f$
In particular, for a module $M \in \operatorname{Mod}^c_A$, the image of $[\operatorname{id}_M]$ is $\chi(M)$.

nodes.name: Topological Hochschild Homology is a shadow
nodes.statement: Topological Hochschild Homology is a shadow. That is, it gives a family of functors \[ \thh (-) \colon \operatorname{Ho}\left(\operatorname{Mod}_{(\mc{C}, \mc{C})}\right) \to \operatorname{Ho}(\operatorname{Sp}) \] that satisfy the required properties.
nodes.statement_short: $\thh$ is a shadow functor on the bicategory of spectral categories.
conclusions: Topological Hochschild Homology is a shadow.
it gives a family of functors \[ \thh (-) \colon \operatorname{Ho}\left(\operatorname{Mod}_{(\mc{C}, \mc{C})}\right) \to \operatorname{Ho}(\operatorname{Sp}) \] that satisfy the required properties

nodes.name: Composite of dual pairs
nodes.statement: If $M_1\in \mc{B}(C,D)$ and $M_2\in \mc{B}(D,E)$ are right dualizable, then $M_1\odot M_2$ is right dualizable. The trace of \[ Q_1\odot M_1\odot M_2\xto{f_1\odot \id_{M_2}} M_1\odot Q_2\odot M_2\xto{\id_{M_1}\odot f_2} M_1\odot M_2\odot Q_3 \] is \[ \sh{Q_1}\xto{\tr(f_1)}\sh{Q_2}\xto{\tr(f_2)}\sh{Q_3}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Right dualizability is closed under $\odot$, and the trace of a composite 2-cell is the composite of the traces.
assumptions: If $M_1\in \mc{B}(C,D)$ and $M_2\in \mc{B}(D,E)$ are right dualizable
conclusions: then $M_1\odot M_2$ is right dualizable
The trace of \[ Q_1\odot M_1\odot M_2\xto{f_1\odot \id_{M_2}} M_1\odot Q_2\odot M_2\xto{\id_{M_1}\odot f_2} M_1\odot M_2\odot Q_3 \] is \[ \sh{Q_1}\xto{\tr(f_1)}\sh{Q_2}\xto{\tr(f_2)}\sh{Q_3}. \]

nodes.name: Base change to one object commutes with traces
nodes.statement: Let $\sC$ and $\sD$ be categories enriched over $\sV$, $c$ be an object of $\mc{C}$, $d$ be an object of $\mc{D}$, $\mc{M}$ be a right dualizable $(\sC,\sD)$-bimodule, and suppose $E_d$ is a Morita equivalence. Let $\mc{Q}$ be a $(\sC,\sC)$-bimodule, $\mc{P}$ be a $(\mc{D},\mc{D})$-bimodule and \[ \phi\colon \mc{Q}\odot \mc{M}\to \mc{M}\odot \mc{P} \] be a natural transformation. Then \begin{equation} \xymatrix@C=70pt{ \sh{_{E_c}\mc{Q}_{E_c}}\ar[d]^{\tr\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_c}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}\right)}\ar[r]^-{\tr({_{E_c}\mc{C}}\odot \phi\odot\mc{D}_{E_d})} &\sh{_{E_d}\mc{P}_{E_d}}\ar[d]^{\tr\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_d}{\mc{D}}{\mc{P}}\right)} \\ \sh{\mc{Q}}\ar[r]^-{\tr(\phi)} &\sh{\mc{P}}} \end{equation} commutes.
nodes.statement_short: Traces computed on a single-object subcategory agree with traces on the whole category, provided $E_d$ is a Morita equivalence.
assumptions: Let $\sC$ and $\sD$ be categories enriched over $\sV$, $c$ be an object of $\mc{C}$, $d$ be an object of $\mc{D}$, $\mc{M}$ be a right dualizable $(\sC,\sD)$-bimodule, and suppose $E_d$ is a Morita equivalence.
Let $\mc{Q}$ be a $(\sC,\sC)$-bimodule, $\mc{P}$ be a $(\mc{D},\mc{D})$-bimodule and \[ \phi\colon \mc{Q}\odot \mc{M}\to \mc{M}\odot \mc{P} \] be a natural transformation.
conclusions: \begin{equation} \xymatrix@C=70pt{ \sh{_{E_c}\mc{Q}_{E_c}}\ar[d]^{\tr\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_c}{\mc{C}}{\mc{Q}}\right)}\ar[r]^-{\tr({_{E_c}\mc{C}}\odot \phi\odot\mc{D}_{E_d})} &\sh{_{E_d}\mc{P}_{E_d}}\ar[d]^{\tr\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_d}{\mc{D}}{\mc{P}}\right)} \\ \sh{\mc{Q}}\ar[r]^-{\tr(\phi)} &\sh{\mc{P}}} \end{equation} commutes.

nodes.name: Restriction-Transfer
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \operatorname{res} \circ \operatorname{trf} = \chi(_fC_f) \colon \thh(A) \to \thh(A)\\ \operatorname{trf} \circ \operatorname{res} = \chi((C_f)\odot (_fC)) \colon \thh(C) \to \thh(C). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Both restriction-transfer composites are Euler characteristics of base change objects.
conclusions: \operatorname{res} \circ \operatorname{trf} = \chi(_fC_f) \colon \thh(A) \to \thh(A)
\operatorname{trf} \circ \operatorname{res} = \chi((C_f)\odot (_fC)) \colon \thh(C) \to \thh(C).

nodes.name: Reidemeister trace of $f$ as the $\thh$ transfer
nodes.statement: The Reidemeister trace of $f\colon X \to X$ is the $\thh$ transfer \[ S \simeq \thh(S) \to \thh(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X;-\sma \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f) \simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} X^f \]
nodes.statement_short: The Reidemeister trace of a self-map is the twisted $\thh$ transfer landing in $\Sigma^\infty_+\mc{L}X^f$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be path-connected space that has the homotopy type of a finite CW-complex, and let $f\colon X \to X$ be a self map.
conclusions: The Reidemeister trace of $f\colon X \to X$ is the $\thh$ transfer \[ S \simeq \thh(S) \to \thh(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X;-\sma \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f) \simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} X^f \]

nodes.name: Inverse of the Morita invariance map via base change
nodes.statement: For a Morita equivalence $E_a\colon \End_{\mc{A}}(a)\to \mc{A}$, an object $b$ of $\mc{A}$, and a map of modules $\alpha\colon 1_{\mc{V}}\to {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{I_b}}$, the trace of \[1_\mc{V}\odot {_{I_b} \mc{A}_{E_a}} \xto{\alpha \odot \id} {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{I_b}}\odot {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{E_a}} \xto{\rbmm{\epsilon}{I_b}{\mc{A}}{U_\mc{A}}{\mc{A}_{E_a}}} {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{E_a}} \] is the composite \[1_{\sV}\xto{\alpha}\mc{A}(b,b) \to \sh{\mc{A}}\xto{\chi_{(\mc{A}_{E_a},{_{E_a}\mc{A}})} (\mc{A}_{E_a})} \sh{\End_{\mc{A}}(a)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: The trace of the action of an endomorphism at $b$ factors as $\alpha$, inclusion into the shadow, then the Euler characteristic implementing the Morita inverse.
assumptions: For a Morita equivalence $E_a\colon \End_{\mc{A}}(a)\to \mc{A}$, an object $b$ of $\mc{A}$, and a map of modules $\alpha\colon 1_{\mc{V}}\to {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{I_b}}$
conclusions: the trace of \[1_\mc{V}\odot {_{I_b} \mc{A}_{E_a}} \xto{\alpha \odot \id} {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{I_b}}\odot {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{E_a}} \xto{\rbmm{\epsilon}{I_b}{\mc{A}}{U_\mc{A}}{\mc{A}_{E_a}}} {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{E_a}} \] is the composite \[1_{\sV}\xto{\alpha}\mc{A}(b,b) \to \sh{\mc{A}}\xto{\chi_{(\mc{A}_{E_a},{_{E_a}\mc{A}})} (\mc{A}_{E_a})} \sh{\End_{\mc{A}}(a)}.\]

nodes.name: $\pi_0$-level cyclotomic trace is the bicategorical trace
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a ring spectrum, and $f\colon M \to M$ an endomorphism of compact $R$-modules. Then the composition \[ S \xrightarrow{f} \operatorname{Mod}^c_R (M, M) \hookrightarrow \bigvee_M \operatorname{Mod}^c_R(M, M) \hookrightarrow \thh (\operatorname{Mod}^c_R) \xrightarrow{\chi} \thh(R) \] coincides with the bicategorical trace $S \to \thh(R)$ induced by $f\colon M \to M$.
nodes.statement_short: The inclusion-of-objects composite defining the $\pi_0$ cyclotomic trace of $f$ equals its bicategorical trace.
assumptions: Let $R$ be a ring spectrum, and $f\colon M \to M$ an endomorphism of compact $R$-modules.
conclusions: Then the composition \[ S \xrightarrow{f} \operatorname{Mod}^c_R (M, M) \hookrightarrow \bigvee_M \operatorname{Mod}^c_R(M, M) \hookrightarrow \thh (\operatorname{Mod}^c_R) \xrightarrow{\chi} \thh(R) \] coincides with the bicategorical trace $S \to \thh(R)$ induced by $f\colon M \to M$.

nodes.name: Twisted cyclic bar construction computes $\mc{L} X^f$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a (connected) topological space. Then \[ B^{\text{cy}}(\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) \simeq \mc{L} X^f \]
nodes.statement_short: The $f$-twisted cyclic bar construction on the Moore loop space is equivalent to the $f$-twisted free loop space.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a (connected) topological space.
conclusions: B^{\text{cy}}(\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) \simeq \mc{L} X^f

nodes.name: Simplified form of $\tr(\rsm{\epsilon}MNP)$ and $\tr(\rsm{\eta}MNQ)$

conclusions: the trace of \[1_\mc{V}\odot {_{F\circ I_a}\mc{M}}\xto{\alpha \odot \id_{{_{F\circ I_a}\mc{M}}}} {_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}\odot {_{F\circ I_a}\mc{M}} \cong {_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}\odot {_{I_a}({_{F}\mc{M}})} \xto{\rbmm{\epsilon}{I_a}{\mc{A}}{U_\mc{A}}{_F\mc{M}}} {_{I_a}({_{F}\mc{M}})}\cong {_{F\circ I_a} \mc{M}}\] as a map of $(1_{\mc{V}},\mc{D})$-bimodules is \[{1_\mc{V}\xto\alpha \sh{{_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}}\xto{\tr(\rbm{\epsilon}{I_a}{\mc{B}}{U_\mc{D}})} \sh{\mc{A}}\xto{\chi(_F\mc{M})} \sh{\mc{D}}. }\]

nodes.name: Folk theorem: cyclotomic trace composite is the Euler characteristic
nodes.origin_citation: folk theorem; Bokstedt, Hsiang, Madsen; Waldhausen
nodes.statement: It is a folk theorem that the composition \begin{equation*} S \xrightarrow{[X]} K(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X) \xrightarrow{\tr} \thh (\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X) \simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} X \to S \end{equation*} is the Euler characteristic.

nodes.name: Functoriality of $\thh$ in the bimodule and category coordinates
nodes.statement: Topological Hochschild homology is clearly functorial in the bimodule coordinate so that given a map of $(\mc{C}, \mc{C})$-bimodules $\mc{Q} \to \mc{Q}'$ there is a map \[ \thh(\mc{C}; \mc{Q}) \to \thh(\mc{C}; \mc{Q}'). \] Furthermore, if $\mc{A} \to \mc{C}$ is a map, then we get an induced map $\thh(\mc{A}) \to \thh(\mc{C})$. There is also a refinement of both \cite{blumberg_mandell}. Let $F\colon \mc{A} \to \mc{C}$ be a map of spectral categories and let $\mc{Q}$ be a $(\mc{C},\mc{C})$-bimodule. Then there is a map \[ \thh(\mc{A};{_F\mc{Q}_F}) \to \thh(\mc{C}, \mc{Q}) \] and if there is a map $\mc{P} \to {_F \mc{Q}_F}$ we obtain \[ \thh(\mc{A}; \mc{P}) \to \thh (\mc{C}, \mc{Q}). \]
nodes.statement_short: $\thh$ is functorial in both coordinates, with a refinement for maps out of a restricted bimodule.

nodes.name: Weak equivalence invariance of $\thh$ in the bimodule coordinate
nodes.statement: Furthermore, by the remark following \cite[Prop.~3.6]{blumberg_mandell}, if $\mc{C}$ is pointwise cofibrant, and $\mc{P} \to \mc{P}'$ is a weak equivalence of spectral categories, then the induced map \[ \thh(\mc{C}, \mc{P}) \to \thh (\mc{C}, \mc{P}') \] is a weak equivalence. Thus, for instance, if $Q\mc{P} \to \mc{P}$ is a cofibrant replacement of $\mc{P}$, $\thh(\mc{C}, Q\mc{P}) \to \thh(\mc{C}, \mc{P})$ is a weak equivalence.
nodes.statement_short: $\thh$ preserves weak equivalences in the bimodule coordinate, so bimodules may be replaced cofibrantly at will.

nodes.name: Cyclic bar construction on the based loop space is the free loop space
nodes.statement: It is a classical fact due to Goodwillie \cite{goodwillie_cyclic} that the cyclic bar construction applied to the based loop space is the free loop space: $B^{\text{cy}} (\Omega X) \simeq \mc{L} X$. nodes.name: Proof that the Reidemeister trace is the twisted transfer
nodes.statement: In \cite[Prop.~3.2.3]{p:thesis} the Reidemeister trace of the introduction is identified with a bicategorical trace. This trace is identified with a more homotopically satisfying trace in \cite[Prop.~6.2.2]{p:thesis} and finally identified with a trace in the parameterized stable homotopy bicategory, $\operatorname{Ex}$, in \cite[Thm.~4.1]{p:coincidence}. In the bicategory of parameterized spectra, let $S_X$ denote the fiberwise suspension spectrum of $X$ regarded as a space over $\ast\times X$ via the identity map. If $f\colon X\to X$ is a continuous map $X_f$ is the fiberwise suspension spectrum of $\{(\gamma,x)\in X^I\times X|\gamma(1)=f(x)\}$ regarded as a space over $X\times X$ via the map $(\gamma,x)\mapsto (\gamma(0),x)$. Then $f$ defines a map of spectra \begin{equation} S \odot S_X \to S_X \odot X_f \end{equation} If $X$ is a closed smooth manifold, $S_X$ is right dualizable and the trace of \eqref{twisted_map_of_X_f} is a map $\sh{S}\to \sh{X_f}$. This map is one form of the Reidemeister trace. Now, we use the Morita equivalence of \cite{lind_malkiewich_morita} to compare the shadows in $\operatorname{Ex}(X, X)$ and $(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X, \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X)$-bimodules. Let $\mc{B}\text{imod}_S$ be the bicategory of ring spectra and spectral bimodules, and $\mc{B}\text{imod}^{\text{gp}}_S$ be the full-subcategory of ring spectra of the form $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X$. Then, \cite[Thm.~6.4]{lind_malkiewich_morita} as applied in \cite[Thm.~5.1]{lind_malkiewich} gives that the parameterized stable homotopy bicategory (when restricted to connected spaces) and $\mc{B}\text{imod}^{\text{gp}}_S$ are bicategorically equivalent with an induced equivalence on shadows. Under this equivalence (given in detail before \cite[Thm.~5.1]{lind_malkiewich}) the map of parameterized spectra in \eqref{twisted_map_of_X_f} passes to the map of $(S, \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X)$-bimodule spectra \begin{equation} S \sma_{S} \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X \to \Sigma^\infty_+\Omega X \sma_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X} \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f. \end{equation} The functoriality of the trace \cite{p:thesis} implies the following diagram commutes. \[ \xymatrix@C=40pt{ \sh{S} \ar[d]^{\sim}\ar[r]^{\tr\eqref{twisted_map_of_X_f} } & \sh{X_f}\ar[d]^{\sim} \\ \sh{S}\ar[r]^-{\tr\eqref{Reidemeister_map_of_modules}} & \sh {\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f}. } \] Then \cref{prop:main_prop} implies \[ \xymatrix{ \sh{S} \ar[d]^{\sim}\ar[r]^-{\tr\eqref{Reidemeister_map_of_modules}} & \sh {\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f}\ar[d]^{\sim}\\ \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_S) \ar[r] & \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X}; -\wedge \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f) } \] commutes and \cref{cor:identify_thh_loop} identifies \[\thh(\Sigma^\infty_+\Omega X; \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f)\simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} X^f .\qedhere\]
nodes.statement_short: Realize the Reidemeister trace as a parameterized bicategorical trace, transport it along the Lind-Malkiewich Morita equivalence, and apply the twisted transfer square plus the appendix computation.
